battle.name: 第二次英藏戰爭
battle.brief: 一八八八年三月，英國以催促履行一八八六年《北京條約》附約為名，遠征軍自印度越過杰萊普山口進入春丕河谷，四月攻入帕里與江孜，設商埠駐兵，藏軍以火繩槍難以擊發而屢退，九月英軍撤回印度；一八九〇年再出兵解江孜之圍。卡面雷管步槍正代表英軍步槍同代的技術世代。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 交戰是三方而非兩方。英方以英屬印度為戰爭機器：加爾各答的印度總督府與倫敦的印度部共同定策，作戰由印度陸軍承擔，出戰部隊包括英軍本土營、廓爾喀營、孟加拉與馬德拉斯正規步兵、皇家炮兵與山地炮兵，以及拉薩的錫金工兵營；第十一孟加拉輕騎兵團負責偵察，後方由大吉嶺喜馬拉雅山鐵路的終點、山麓的馱運站與數千名挑夫接續。英方自認對西藏只有貿易權而無主權，卻在談判中反覆要求條約權利與道路通行。藏方以拉薩的噶倫會議為最高行政，攝政與達賴喇嘛居於政教合一的核心，軍事力量是各地本孜民兵、寺院武裝僧團，以及各地方貴族與總管的私兵，外加自中國、尼泊爾與邊境商路購得的火器；藏方在政治上不承認英國有權單方面與西藏締約。第三方是清廷：光緒帝依例派駐藏辦事大臣坐鎮拉薩，駐藏清軍與邊界綠營由大臣節制，兩江總督等疆臣以電報與拉薩往來。清廷的立場是西藏一切對外條約必須以中國的名義訂立，英國若要推進商路，就必須先越過北京。這正是這場戰爭在外交上三張牌同時打出的原因。
countriesEn: Three parties were involved, not two. On the British side the war machine was British India: the viceroy's government at Calcutta and the India Office in London shared the direction of affairs, and the fighting was done by the Army of India. The expedition drew on British line battalions, Gurkha battalions, Bengal and Madras native infantry, the Royal Artillery with its mountain batteries, and a Sikkim pioneer company for engineering; the 11th Bengal Lancers did the reconnaissance, while at the rear the terminus of the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, the mule stations along the Himalayan foothills and several thousand coolies kept the force supplied. The British claimed no sovereignty over Tibet, only trading rights, and yet in every negotiation they pressed for treaty privileges and for right of way. On the Tibetan side the supreme civil authority was the kashag council at Lhasa, with the regent and the Dalai Lama at the centre of a government that fused religious and secular power. Its military strength was made up of local militia levies, the armed monk troops of the great monasteries, and the private retinues of noble families and district governors, with muskets bought from China, from Nepal and along the border trade routes. Tibet denied that Britain had any right to conclude a treaty with Tibet on its own. The third party was the Qing court: the Guangxu emperor, as custom required, kept an amban at Lhasa, and the garrison stationed in Tibet and the frontier Green Standard troops were under his authority, with the viceroys of the coastal provinces corresponding with Lhasa by telegraph. The Qing position was that every treaty Tibet concluded with a foreign power had to be made in the name of China, so that if Britain wanted its road it had to go through Peking first. That is why this war was fought with three sets of cards in play at once.
people: 關鍵人物集中在三方。藏方的十三世達賴喇嘛（1876–1933）在一八八八年只有十二歲，實權在攝政與噶倫之手，敗績的責任也落在噶倫會議身上；攝政一職此時先後由數人出任，其中最關鍵的是策彭·沙克巴（Tsepon W. D. Shakabpa），他既是噶倫的核心人物，也是此後代表西藏赴印英談判、於一八九三年簽訂《藏英通商章程》的首席代表。英方的戰場指揮官是查士維·葛拉咸（General Sir Charles Graham），他率領一八八八年遠征軍越過山口攻入江孜，兵力部署與撤退時機都出自他手；隨軍英官之中，日後長期駐任江孜的商務代表是查士維·貝爾（Charles A. Bell）。清廷方面，一八九〇年與英國交涉的是陸宏章，他代表光緒帝與印度總督府簽訂條約；駐藏辦事大臣與駐藏清軍的將領則在拉薩主持對英方使節的接待與對峙。一八九〇年英方的談判代表是莫蒂默·杜蘭（Sir Mortimer Durand）。此外，十三世達賴的兄弟、哲蚌寺與色拉寺的僧團首領，以及拉孜、日喀則等地方勢力的頭人，都在各自的圈內決定了守城、退走還是議和的姿態；地方頭人各自打各自的算盤，往往正是英軍得以逐點推進的縫隙所在。
peopleEn: The decisive personalities fall into the three parties. The Thirteenth Dalai Lama (1876–1933) was only twelve years old in 1888; real power lay with the regent and the kashag, and so did the blame for defeat. The office of regent passed through several hands in these years, and the most consequential of them was Tsepon W. D. Shakabpa, a leading member of the kashag and later the chief Tibetan representative in the negotiations with British India, the man who signed the Anglo-Tibetan Trade Regulations in 1893. On the British side the field commander was General Sir Charles Graham, who led the expedition of 1888 over the passes into Gyantse and decided both the deployment of the troops and the timing of the withdrawal; among the British officials with the force, the man who would later sit for years at Gyantse as Trade Agent was Charles A. Bell. On the Qing side the negotiator of 1890 was Lu Hongzhang, who signed for the Guangxu emperor and the viceroy's government, while the amban in Lhasa and the commanders of the garrison there handled the reception of, and the confrontation with, the British emissaries. Britain's negotiator in 1890 was Sir Mortimer Durand. Alongside them the Dalai Lama's brother, the heads of the great monasteries of Drepung and Sera, and the chiefs of the local houses at Shigatse and Gyantse each decided, within their own circle, whether to hold the town, to withdraw or to talk; the local chiefs each calculating their own advantage were themselves the seam through which the British advanced point by point. The scattered command structure of the Tibetan side, and the fact that the monasteries, the militia and the noble households drew their strength from different districts, meant that a victory at one point rarely became a pursuit to the next.
kits: 卡面這支雷管步槍是法國一八四〇年式的雷管點火步槍，它本身並沒有出現在一八八八年的西藏戰場上；但它代表的是英軍步槍同屬的技術世代：雷管取代火燧，槍機不再依賴火繩濺出的火星，鋼製後膛承受得住較大的膛壓，配上紙殼藥包與銅帽，裝填與擊發都快了許多，一八四〇年代法國率先普及的紙殼藥包正是英國日後模仿的對象。英軍在此役真正使用的主武器是瑪提尼·亨利槍（Martini-Henry，一八七一年式，.577 黑火藥），一八八八年起才逐步換裝的萊-梅特福德連發步槍（Lee-Metford，.303）則屬同一世代的下一代；機關槍是 Maxim 機槍，炮兵配七磅與九磅口徑的野戰炮，山地炮兵連另配小口徑山地炮與曲射炮。英軍真正的難題在後勤：從加爾各答經大吉嶺、錫金到乃堆拉山口（杰萊普山口）是一條逾兩百公里的山地補給線，全靠騾、牦牛、雪橇與數千名挑夫維持，彈藥箱的重量直接決定推進速度。藏方的火力核心是火繩槍與燧發槍，火器數量雖多，卻雜亂而缺乏制式，銅帽與火藥仰賴進口，應急時甚至以自製火繩湊合；弓矢、長刀與長矛仍在部分守備單位配發，少數幾門老式滑膛炮佈在江孜與帕里一帶的土堡中。真正決定射程與命中率的，正是卡面步槍所代表的東西：雷管在嚴寒、乾燥、風沙的高原上照樣擊發，火繩槍在同一環境裡常常點不着火。
kitsEn: The rifle on this card is the French percussion musket of 1840, and it did not itself appear on the Tibetan battlefield in 1888; but it stands for the same technical generation as the infantry rifle the British carried. Percussion had displaced the flint, the lock no longer depended on a spark from a match, a steel breech withstood the higher chamber pressures, and the paper cartridge with its fulminate cap made loading and firing quicker; the paper cartridge first put into general use by France in the 1840s was the very thing Britain afterwards copied. The main weapon actually used by the British in this campaign was the Martini-Henry rifle of the 1871 pattern in .577 black powder, while the newly adopted Lee-Metford magazine rifle in .303, which began to replace it from 1888, belonged to the next step of the same generation; the machine gun was the Maxim, and the artillery batteries carried field guns of the 7-pounder and 9-pounder classes, with the mountain batteries using small-calibre mountain guns and howitzers. The real difficulty for the British was logistics. From Calcutta by Darjeeling and Sikkim to the Jelep La ran a mountain supply line of more than two hundred kilometres, kept going on mules, yaks, sledges and several thousand coolies, and the weight of the ammunition boxes set the speed of the advance. The centre of Tibetan firepower was the matchlock and the flintlock. The Tibetans had a great many muskets, but they were of mixed types and had no standard issue, their caps and powder came from outside, and in an emergency they fell back on home-made matches; bows, swords and spears were still distributed to some units, and a few old smooth-bore guns stood in the earthworks at Gyantse and Phari. What really settled the range and the accuracy of fire was the thing the card stands for: a percussion cap will fire in the cold, dry wind of the plateau, while a matchlock in the same conditions often will not light at all.
tactics: 英軍的戰法由後勤決定。它先把攻勢當成一條線來鋪：工程兵開路，清出山口的碎石與積雪，兵站、倉儲與野戰醫院設在每一處據點，步槍營在行軍縱隊兩側散開警戒，運輸隊夾在中間，而不是集中成一個大縱隊。進入春丕河谷後，藏軍利用兩側山壁與狹長谷地據險；英軍的進攻次序是先以炮兵對堡壘與村寨射擊，再用連續正面進攻吸引火力，同時由工兵小隊沿山脊迂迴，切斷守軍退路，逼其放棄石築寨牆與土堡。撤退與進攻同樣有紀律：一八八八年秋，英軍在給養耗盡與冬季封山之前主動撤出江孜，把商務代表與重要物資先行運回印度，而不是戀戰；翌年再以同一條補給線派遣救援軍，於一八九〇年春在帕里拉與洋則一帶與藏軍主力交戰，迫使包圍江孜的藏軍解圍撤退。藏軍的戰術則圍繞不與英軍決戰：在帕里宗與江孜一線築壘固守，以火繩槍齊射，擊退英軍前哨即退入後方；夜襲英軍營地與護衛，專打運輸隊與通訊隊，切斷山口以上的道路，把英軍的推進速度拖到糧秣所允許的極限。此外，藏軍的僧團、本孜民兵與地方私兵指揮系統互不相屬，同一場戰役裡往往各自退守，這使他們難以集中兵力，也讓一八八八年的進攻在打到江孜時已失去銳氣。
tacticsEn: The British way of war was dictated by their logistics. They treated the advance as a line to be built: engineers cleared the passes of rock and snow, depots, magazines and field hospitals were established at every occupied place, the rifle companies opened out on both flanks of the marching column to keep the way, and the transport trains ran in the middle rather than massed in one grand column. Once in the Chumbi Valley the Tibetans used the narrowness of the gorge and the walls of the hills on either side to hold their ground. The British order of attack was to bring the guns onto the forts and villages first, then apply continuous frontal pressure to fix the defenders, while engineer detachments worked along the ridge line to cut the retreat and force the garrison out of its stone walls and earthen defences. Withdrawal was governed by the same discipline as the advance: in the autumn of 1888 the British left Gyantse of their own accord before stores ran out and the passes closed for the winter, taking the trade agent and the bulk of the stores back to India rather than trying to hold on; the following year the same line of supply carried a relief force which in the spring of 1890 fought the main Tibetan body near Phari La and at Yangtse, compelling the Tibetans to lift the blockade of Gyantse and withdraw. Tibetan tactics turned on refusing a decisive battle. They fortified Phari Dzong and the line back to Gyantse, fired massed volleys of matchlocks, and fell back on the raiders as soon as the British forward posts were checked; they attacked the camp by night, went after supply columns and communications parties, and cut the road above the Jelep La, dragging the British advance down to the limit their rations allowed. The monk troops, the local militia and the private bands of the nobility were under separate commands and did not answer to one another, so that even when they held a position they could not concentrate for the next one; by the time the fighting reached Gyantse in 1888 their offensive force had already spent itself.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。遠征始於一八八八年三月，部隊自大吉嶺與加爾各答出發，穿越錫金，於三月底越過乃堆拉山口，海拔約四千二百七十公尺；四月攻入帕里宗，海拔約四千一百公尺，再沿約四十公里的路線進抵江孜，海拔約四千二百公尺，英軍於四月下旬佔領江孜並設商埠，至九月主動撤出。一八九〇年四月救援軍再次越過山口，同年六月初解除江孜之圍，撤退在夏季完成，未在海拔四千公尺以上過冬。作戰部隊方面，兩次英軍出動均為數千人量級，隨軍挑夫與馱手另有數千人，總行程逾兩百公里；藏軍在江孜一線集結的兵力在數千人上下，寺院與地方方面的說法常有數萬之眾，無可靠核對。裝備方面，英軍步槍以瑪提尼·亨利槍為主，配機關槍數挺、七磅與九磅野戰炮十餘門、小口徑山地炮數門；藏軍火繩槍數千支，老式滑膛炮十數門，銅帽與火藥靠進口。傷亡方面，英軍作戰部隊的陣亡與失蹤在數百人量級，藏軍損失以數千計，兩造皆無逐日可核的名冊。距離與時間還有一組要點：江孜至拉薩尚有約二百七十公里，其間尚有數道山口，英軍從未走完這條路，遠征始終止步於江孜以東。最後是條約的日期：一八九〇年八月十七日《中英藏條約》在京簽訂，一八九一年互換批准書，一八九三年《藏英通商章程》在加爾各答簽訂。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The expedition began in March 1888. The column left Darjeeling and Calcutta, crossed Sikkim and went over the Jelep La at the end of March, at about 4,270 metres; Phari Dzong, at roughly 4,100 metres, was taken in April, and the advance continued by a road of some forty kilometres to Gyantse, at about 4,200 metres, which the British occupied in the second half of April and where a trade mart was set up. They withdrew in September of their own accord. In April 1890 the relief force crossed the passes again, relieved Gyantse in early June, and completed its withdrawal before the winter, spending no season above four thousand metres. As for numbers of men, the British went out on both occasions with a fighting force of the order of a few thousand, with several thousand more coolies and muleteers, over a total march of more than two hundred kilometres; the Tibetans concentrated something of the order of a few thousand men on the Gyantse line, while temple and local reports claimed tens of thousands, none of which could be checked. In equipment the British infantry were armed mainly with Martini-Henry rifles, with a few machine guns, a dozen or more field guns of the 7-pounder and 9-pounder classes and a handful of small mountain guns; the Tibetans had several thousand matchlocks, a dozen or so old smooth-bore guns, and imported caps and powder. In losses the killed and missing of the British fighting force ran to hundreds and the Tibetan losses to thousands, and neither side kept a roll that can be checked day by day. Distance and time supply a further set of figures: about 270 kilometres separate Gyantse from Lhasa, with several more passes on the way, and the British never walked that road; their expedition stopped east of Gyantse. The dates of the settlement are the last set: the Anglo-Chinese Convention on Tibet was signed at Peking on 17 August 1890, the ratifications were exchanged in 1891, and the Anglo-Tibetan Trade Regulations were signed at Calcutta in 1893.
cause: 起因由三層組成。最外層是條約義務：一八八四年中英在加爾各答訂立的藏英商約把藏地對外貿易限定由英國經營，並同意在江孜設商埠，一八八六年《北京條約》確認英國對這項壟斷權的保護，英國據此要求修通一條由印度經春丕河谷直抵江孜的道路，並派兵護送。藏方以噶倫會議與幾座大寺否決任何讓路，理由是條約從未經達賴與噶倫同意，也不願讓英軍隊伍長期駐紮在通向拉薩的走廊上。中層是英國的安全盤算：一八八〇年代英國在喜馬拉雅的戰略是先把通往拉薩的道路測量清楚並可隨時走通，作為對付俄國勢力自中亞南下的長線準備，同時防範錫金與不丹方向的邊境爭端；道路因此不是工程，而是戰略資產。內層則是清廷與藏方的分歧：清廷堅持西藏對外的一切條約都由北京出面訂立，藏方卻在部分對外事務上繞過清廷自行應對，英國正好利用這一縫隙，試圖在拉薩與倫敦之間直接建立關係。一八八八年二月英方提出的最後通牒要求限期開路並撤走阻路的藏軍，期限屆滿而藏方未從，遠征便在三月展開。
causeEn: The causes fall into three layers. The outermost is the treaty obligation. The 1884 Trade Convention concluded between Britain and Tibet at Calcutta reserved Tibet's foreign trade to Britain and provided for a British trade mart at Gyantse, and the Convention of Peking of 1886 affirmed the protection of that monopoly. On that footing Britain demanded a road from India through the Chumbi Valley straight to Gyantse, and troops to guard it. The kashag council and the great monasteries refused any cession of the way, on the ground that the treaty had never been accepted by the Dalai Lama or the kashag, and they were unwilling to see foreign soldiers quartered for long in the corridor that leads to Lhasa. The middle layer is British strategy. In the 1880s the object of British policy on the Himalaya was to have the road to Lhasa surveyed and passable at will, as a long preparation against Russian influence coming down from Central Asia, and to settle border disputes in the direction of Sikkim and Bhutan; the road was therefore not a work of engineering but a strategic asset. The innermost layer is the disagreement between the Qing court and the Tibetans. The Qing insisted that every treaty Tibet made abroad must be made at Peking, while the Tibetans in some matters dealt with outsiders without instructions from Beijing, and Britain used exactly that seam to try to establish a direct relation between Lhasa and London. The ultimatum of February 1888 demanded that the road be opened and the obstructing Tibetan troops withdrawn by a fixed date; when the date passed without compliance, the expedition began in March.
impact: 戰爭的直接後果是把西藏推入近代國際關係：清廷在一八九〇年被迫與英國直接訂約，形式上保住中國對西藏有宗主權的名義，實際上承認了英國在西藏的宗主權與在江孜的常駐權力；藏英之間更在一八九三年訂立通商章程，英方的商務代表、旅居權、傳教權與印鑄貨幣權被寫進文件，藏方拒絕接受其中多項，雙方爭執延續到二十世紀初，直接導致一九〇四年英軍遠征拉薩與其後的邊界劃定。對英國而言收益極為可觀：喜馬拉雅山脈南麓的主動權到手，去加爾各答的路線、靠印度人力物力的補給體系，以及廓爾喀營在高原作戰的經驗，都在一八九〇年代成形，英國在印度的邊防由守住一條線變成向線內推進。對藏方，損失在於對外自主與內部威信：噶倫會議在敗局中分裂，拉薩的寺院武裝被解散，地方本孜與貴族私兵的戰力被削弱，攝政與噶倫在往後二十年的權力鬥爭中更形尖銳。對清廷而言，則是宗主權的空洞化與持續的銀錢支出，被迫在中英之間維持既不完全接受、也不正面拒絕的中間狀態，這個狀態一直延續到清末。國際層面上，這場戰爭是大博弈的一個節點：英國在此確認西藏不屬俄國勢力範圍，俄國其後也承認英國在西藏的立場，喜馬拉雅的勢力分割自此定型。
impactEn: The immediate consequence was to thrust Tibet into modern international relations. The Qing court was forced into direct treaty with Britain in 1890, keeping the formula that China held suzerainty over Tibet while in practice accepting British suzerainty and a permanent British agency at Gyantse; the Trade Regulations of 1893 went further still, writing commercial representation, residence, missionary activity and the right of coinage into the text, and the Tibetans refused to accept several of these clauses. The dispute over them ran into the opening years of the twentieth century and led directly to the British expedition to Lhasa of 1904 and to the drawing of the frontier line that followed. For Britain the returns were considerable: initiative on the southern side of the Himalaya, a road to Calcutta worked with Indian men and money, and experience of Gurkha battalions fighting on high ground, all of which shaped British frontier policy in India during the 1890s, turning the defence of a line into advance beyond it. For Tibet the losses were in external autonomy and internal standing: the kashag was split by the defeat, the armed monastic troops of Lhasa were disbanded, and the fighting strength of the local militia and the noble retinues was reduced, sharpening the power struggle between regents and ministers over the following two decades. For the Qing the effect was the hollowing out of suzerainty and the steady drain of silver, since it had to hold a middle position between acceptance and refusal that lasted until the end of the dynasty. At the level of world politics the war was a round of the Great Game: Britain settled that Tibet lay outside the Russian sphere, Russia in turn accepted the British position, and the partition of the Himalaya was fixed.
result: 結果可以分軍事、政治與象徵三層。軍事上，藏軍在江孜與帕里一線的抵抗迫使英軍在一八八八年放棄據守，撤退回印度；英國並未在那一役消滅藏軍主力，戰役的果實不在戰場而在條約。政治上，一八九〇年八月十七日陸宏章與莫蒂默·杜蘭在北京簽訂《中英藏條約》，確認英國對西藏的宗主權與中國對西藏的宗主權並存，一八九一年互換批准書；一八九三年《藏英通商章程》由沙克巴與貝爾在加爾各答簽訂，規定商埠管理、旅居、傳教、郵政與印鑄貨幣等條款，藏方事實上接受了一套對英不平等的制度。一八九〇年的救援軍在帕里拉與洋則一帶擊退藏軍主力，解除江孜之圍後即撤出，沒有攻向拉薩。象徵上，藏軍解體，僧團武裝被遣散，地方軍頭失去影響力，噶倫政府轉而倚重英方供給的少量武器與訓練維持秩序；同年攝政更替，達賴喇嘛於一八九二年親政，拉薩對外政策更趨保守與封閉。這場戰爭留下的最大問題，是條約在西藏內地從未真正落實：英國發現商路不通、傳教士無從進入、藏方對各條款消極抵制，一八九〇年代末期矛盾重新累積，一九〇四年英軍以保護之名出兵拉薩，比這一役走得更遠。
resultEn: The result divides into military, political and symbolic layers. Militarily, the Tibetan stand at Gyantse and Phari forced the British to give up the occupied post and withdraw to India in 1888; the British did not destroy the main Tibetan force, and the fruit of the campaign lay in the treaty, not on the field. Politically, on 17 August 1890 Lu Hongzhang and Sir Mortimer Durand signed the Anglo-Chinese Convention on Tibet at Peking, confirming British suzerainty over Tibet alongside Chinese suzerainty, and the ratifications were exchanged in 1891; the Anglo-Tibetan Trade Regulations were signed at Calcutta in 1893 by Shakabpa and Bell, defining the management of the trade mart, residence, missionary activity, the postal service and the coinage of money, and the Tibetans in practice accepted a system that was unequal in British favour. The relief force of 1890 defeated the main Tibetan body near Phari La and at Yangtse, relieved Gyantse and withdrew without advancing on Lhasa. Symbolically, the Tibetan army was broken up, the monastic levies were sent home, the local commanders lost their influence, and the kashag government came to rely on a small supply of British weapons and training to keep order; the regency changed hands in the same year, and in 1892 the Dalai Lama took power in person, after which the foreign policy of Lhasa grew more conservative and closed. The largest problem left behind was that the treaty was never really carried out in the interior of Tibet: the British found the road unusable, the missionaries unable to enter and the Tibetans passively resisting every clause, and in the late 1890s the grievance accumulated again, until in 1904 the British marched on Lhasa under the banner of protection, going further than they had in this war.
